body:
The problem with “just use ChatGPT”

Generative AI is already in most Australian workplaces, often through personal accounts. Staff use it to draft emails, summarise documents and write proposals. That brings real productivity, but also real risks: client information pasted into public tools, inconsistent quality, confident but wrong answers and no record of what was shared. The OAIC’s guidance on privacy and commercially available AI products recommends that organisations do not enter personal or sensitive information into publicly available generative AI tools.

Generative AI consulting keeps the productivity and removes the risk. Your team gets approved tools, configured properly, with clear rules and ready-made prompts for the work they actually do.

What our generative AI consulting covers

1. Use-case discovery

We interview each team to find the tasks where generative AI helps most: drafting, summarising, research, reporting, customer replies, proposals, policy writing and data analysis. We also note tasks where it shouldn’t be used.

2. Tool selection

We compare tools against your needs and existing software. If you run Microsoft 365, Copilot may fit naturally; for writing and analysis, Claude or ChatGPT business plans may suit better; Google Workspace users may prefer Gemini. We look at data settings, admin controls, cost per user and integrations.

3. Secure configuration

We set up business accounts with single sign-on where available, data-use settings that keep your content out of model training where the provider offers it, workspace sharing rules and admin oversight.

4. Policy and guardrails

We write a short AI usage policy: approved tools, what may and may not be shared, when outputs need human review, how to disclose AI use to clients and who to ask. It aligns with Australia’s AI Ethics Principles and the Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption.

5. Prompt libraries and custom assistants

Each team receives tested prompts for its common tasks, plus custom assistants (such as GPTs, Claude Projects or Copilot agents) loaded with your templates, tone of voice and reference material.

6. Training and measurement

We run practical sessions with each team and track adoption and time saved over the following weeks. For deeper skills development, see AI training for teams.

Generative AI tools compared

ToolStrengthsOften suits
Microsoft CopilotWorks inside Word, Outlook, Excel and Teams with your Microsoft dataBusinesses standardised on Microsoft 365
ChatGPT business plansBroad capability, custom GPTs, strong ecosystemGeneral drafting, analysis and custom assistants
ClaudeLong documents, careful writing and analysis, Projects for shared contextPolicy, legal-style and report-heavy work
Google GeminiBuilt into Gmail, Docs and SheetsGoogle Workspace organisations

Many organisations use more than one. The policy matters more than the brand.

From tools to workflows

The biggest gains come when generative AI moves from individual chats into repeatable workflows, such as a proposal process that drafts from your CRM notes, or a weekly report that writes itself. When a use case proves valuable, we can automate it through AI workflow automation or build a dedicated assistant with AI integration.

How the engagement runs

  1. Free AI audit to understand your teams and current AI use.
  2. Discovery and tool selection over one to two weeks.
  3. Configuration, policy and prompt libraries.
  4. Training sessions on site in Melbourne or online.
  5. Follow-up review after four to six weeks to measure adoption and refine.

Generative AI use cases by team

  • Sales: account research, tailored proposals and follow-up emails drafted from CRM notes.
  • Marketing: content outlines, campaign variations and repurposing long content into posts, in your brand voice.
  • Operations: procedures, checklists and summaries of long email threads or meeting notes.
  • Finance: commentary on monthly figures and help with spreadsheet formulas, always checked by a person.
  • Customer service: reply drafts and knowledge-base articles that match your policies.

Each use case gets a tested prompt and a note on what the person must check before using the output.

We review the policy and prompt library with you after the first month and update both as tools and needs change.
faqs: Is it safe to use ChatGPT for business in Australia?

It can be, with the right setup. Use a business plan with appropriate data settings, follow a clear usage policy, and avoid entering personal or sensitive information into public AI tools, as the OAIC recommends.
Should we choose Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?

It depends on your existing software and the work your teams do. Microsoft 365 users often start with Copilot, Google Workspace users with Gemini, and writing-heavy teams often prefer Claude or ChatGPT. We compare them against your needs.
Do we need an AI usage policy?
Yes. A short policy tells staff which tools are approved, what information must never be shared and when AI output needs human review. It protects clients and makes AI use consistent.
How quickly will staff see results from generative AI?
Most teams save time within the first few weeks once they have approved tools, ready-made prompts and a short training session. We measure adoption and time saved in a follow-up review.
